claim: On packet v5 at measured speciation, refits weighted by Hilliard's stated measurement uncertainties plus the project's +-5 % carbamate assumption give SSM+DS a lower chi-square than original Born in every case: three uniform carbamate scales, measured and nominal states, with and without a loading-linear carbamate bias, and on the Hilliard Appendix F NMR holdout without refitting. The difference is 0.3-1.3 chi-square units, below the decisive threshold of 10 even when the weights are shrunk to the observed scatter, so the order is consistent but not decisive. SSM stays rejected on physical grounds: implausible ion-solvent unlike energies and negative packet-coordinate aqueous osmotic coefficients at k_ij=0. No packet coordinates are changed. Packet v5 here states original Born (c_shell = c_dielectric = 0). The MEA-Thermodynamics application does not: its selected record omits both coefficients and its shared_evaluation.py fills (1, 1), so the application evaluates SSM+DS (MEA-Thermodynamics PR #125, check N1). The MEA Born-form decision belongs to MEA-Thermodynamics #121 decision 21.

diagnosed_cause_of_remaining_negative: With the two ion-solvent k_ij fitted, the admissible Born forms differ in these partial pressures by less than their measurement and speciation uncertainty. At Hilliard's stated uncertainties the reduced chi-square is 0.30-0.54: water rows carry 2.2 % against about 0.8 % observed scatter, and MEA rows at high loading are dominated by speciation and loading uncertainty. The fitted k_ij absorb the unfitted Born-form slope difference. Partial pressures at matched speciation do not separate the forms while k_ij are free, also without the carbamate term in the weights; data that fix the ion-solvent interaction independently can. Density cannot help: it is Born-blind in this model.
domain: 30 wt% MEA, 313.15 and 333.15 K, 6.6-22 kPa, CO2 loading 0.15-0.49 mol/mol
